scope: Exploratory colored-object factorization on failed Hand2Dex raw outputs
summary: Source-object factorization substantially improved case 2 object and motion scores but did not repair temporal consistency; case 3 tracking failed to improve the apple and regressed temporal quality.
evidence: Case 2 object consistency improved from 0.653830 to 0.876721 and motion from 0.785458 to 0.876785; identity remained 0.980508.
Case 2 temporal consistency improved only from 0.246224 to 0.277606, leaving the complete gate failed.
Case 3 object consistency remained 0.003866 while temporal consistency fell from 0.311885 to 0.190041.
The repair is explicitly separated from the raw-model leaderboard and uses source-video pixels.
lessons: Object factorization can fix a dominant colored-object failure when tracking is reliable.
A 2-D color tracker does not generalize uniformly across objects and cannot solve temporal robot morphology.
Object restoration and temporal generation are separate mechanisms and require separate controls.
limitations: The repair was explored after viewing raw test failures and is not confirmation evidence.
It is deterministic image-space compositing, not learned transfer or physical interaction.
Case 1 was not rerun in this exploratory round.
next_actions: Develop object/contact masks on a separate training/validation object set, then freeze the tracker before confirmation.
Pair object factorization with a geometry-aware temporal generator rather than post-hoc global smoothing.
